newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil--low sulphur jumps, high sulphur sits.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil--low sulphur jumps, high sulphur sits.

text.p: Low sulphur cracked fuel jumped higher on Wednesday boosted by thinner supplies in NWE, colder weather in the U.S and tighter tonnage, while high sulphur drifted sideways on cargoes and edged down for barges.

"Cold weather in the U.S has made gas expensive compared with fuel, so people are buying fuel," said a trader. American supplies of low sulphur cracked cargoes are expected to be sold locally and the increased demand may also draw fuel from Europe.
Two 45-50kt cargoes moved Tuesday, leaving only one similar sized cargo available in November. Traders said people were now looking for winter supplies and questioning where fuel was.
"It's the highest since the Gulf War," said one dealer.

High sulphur cargoes drifted sideways -- pegged broadly unchanged around $107 fob NWE -- in very quiet trade. Barges actually lost ground with $113.50 fob ARA the highest trade and with as low as $111.50 done. Traders said there was slack buying interest and more than enough material to meet the poor demand.
